advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether created output parent directories should also be cleaned up on failure, or document that they are intentionally left in place.
evidence: infra/scripts/prepare_reclaim_backup.py:303: `bundle.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`
infra/scripts/prepare_reclaim_backup.py:329: `for artifact in (bundle, manifest):`
infra/scripts/prepare_reclaim_backup.py:332: `artifact.unlink()`
advisory.finding: On any failure after bundle.parent/manifest.parent are created, the finally block unlinks only the bundle and manifest files but leaves the freshly created (possibly empty) parent directory trees behind, since mkdir(parents=True) is not rolled back.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that passes an --old-tip differing from live refs/heads/tickets and asserts failure with the mismatch message.
evidence: source: `if tickets.direct_oid != args.old_tip: raise ReclaimError("--old-tip differs from the initial live refs/heads/tickets OID")`
test `_run` always passes `fixture.old_tip` (tests/integration/test_prepare_reclaim_backup.py:170-171), which is asserted to equal live tickets in the fixture — no test supplies a divergent --old-tip
ABSENCE: no test asserts a nonzero exit / this error message for a stale --old-tip
advisory.finding: The `--old-tip` mismatch guard in `prepare()` (raises 'differs from the initial live refs/heads/tickets OID' when `tickets.direct_oid != args.old_tip`) has no test. Every test passes `fixture.old_tip`, which equals the live `refs/heads/tickets` OID, so the mismatch branch never executes; a regression removing this safety check (backing up against a tip that no longer matches live) would not be caught.
scenarios: operator reruns with a stale --old-tip after tickets advanced

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that mutates origin (e.g. pushes a new tag) after the initial snapshot and asserts the 'snapshot changed' failure with cleanup.
evidence: source: `if _remote_snapshot(repo) != initial_snapshot: raise ReclaimError("remote heads/tags snapshot changed before backup completion")`
ABSENCE: tests assert remote snapshot is unchanged (test line 229, 323) but none pushes/deletes a remote ref during the run to trigger the guard's failure path
advisory.finding: The final TOCTOU re-check ('remote heads/tags snapshot changed before backup completion') is untested. No test mutates the origin between the initial `_remote_snapshot` and the final one, so the re-snapshot comparison branch never fires; a regression deleting the final snapshot comparison would pass all current tests.
scenarios: origin refs change concurrently while the backup is preparing

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests passing a non-commit pin (blob-pin) and a non-ref pin argument, asserting the distinct 'is not a commit' / 'must name a ref' errors.
evidence: source `_commit_oid`: `raise ReclaimError(f"{label} is not a commit: {ref}")` and `... is missing locally ...`
source `_resolve_pins`: `if not canonical.startswith("refs/"): raise ReclaimError(f"--pin-ref must name a ref: {requested}")`
test `_run` only ever passes `--pin-ref refs/tags/annotated-pin` and `--pin-ref refs/tags/local-pin` (tests/integration/test_prepare_reclaim_backup.py:175-179), both commits
ABSENCE: no test passes a blob/non-commit or non-ref pin and asserts the corresponding error
advisory.finding: The `--pin-ref` resolution error paths in `_resolve_pins`/`_commit_oid` are untested: neither the 'is not a commit' branch (a non-commit pin such as the fixture's `refs/tags/blob-pin`) nor the 'must name a ref' branch (a non-ref argument) is exercised. The blob-pin object exists in the fixture but is only observed via manifest `relationship == 'non-commit'`, never passed as a `--pin-ref`.
scenarios: operator pins a blob or a bare non-ref string

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test against an origin lacking refs/heads/tickets (and/or empty origin) asserting the corresponding parse/guard errors.
evidence: source raises: 'malformed git ls-remote snapshot', 'unexpected peeled remote ref', 'unexpected remote ref', 'duplicate remote ref in snapshot', 'origin has no heads or tags to snapshot', 'peeled tag lacks direct row'
source prepare(): `if tickets is None: raise ReclaimError("origin snapshot has no refs/heads/tickets")`
ABSENCE: no test drives origin into an empty/malformed/tickets-less state (e.g. a remote without refs/heads/tickets) to exercise these guards
advisory.finding: `_parse_remote_refs` validation branches and the missing-tickets guard are untested. The malformed-snapshot, duplicate-ref, unexpected-ref, dangling-peeled-tag, empty-snapshot errors, and the 'origin snapshot has no refs/heads/tickets' guard have no coverage — the fixture always produces a well-formed snapshot containing refs/heads/tickets.
scenarios: origin missing the tickets branch; empty origin; unexpected ref namespaces

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests that (a) dirty the source worktree and (b) use a shallow clone, each asserting the appropriate refusal.
evidence: source `_assert_safe_clone`: raises 'backup source worktree is not clean' and 'shallow clone is unsafe; use a fresh unfiltered clone'
covered branches: partial clone (test line 234) and existing refs/reclaim-backup/ (test line 372)
ABSENCE: no test makes the worktree dirty or uses a shallow clone (`git clone --depth 1`) and asserts the refusal
advisory.finding: The shallow-clone and dirty-worktree refusals in `_assert_safe_clone` are untested; only the partial-clone and stale-helper-ref safety branches have coverage.
scenarios: operator runs against a dirty checkout or a --depth-limited clone

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm _verify_restore's exact bundle-ref equality holds when two --pin-ref args resolve to the same commit OID (add a test or dedup helper refs by OID).
evidence: infra/scripts/prepare_reclaim_backup.py:254: `if _bundle_heads(repo, bundle) != bundle_refs:`
infra/scripts/prepare_reclaim_backup.py:227: `for index, oid in enumerate(pins, 1):`

ABSENCE: tests/integration/test_prepare_reclaim_backup.py only pins annotated-pin (ancestor) and local-pin (diverged) plus old-tip — three distinct OIDs; no test covers two pins resolving to the same commit.
dropped.finding: When two --pin-ref arguments resolve to the same commit OID, _create_helper_refs creates two distinct helper refs (pin-1, pin-2) pointing at one object; _verify_restore then requires _bundle_heads(bundle) to equal bundle_refs exactly. If `git bundle create`/`list-heads` collapses or reorders same-OID refs, the equality check `_bundle_heads(repo, bundle) != bundle_refs` could spuriously fail. This duplicate-OID case is not exercised by any test (the fixture uses three distinct OIDs).
